subject: what size of data do others have experience with using rhipe?

messages.author: 2f3428d3166aad1c
messages.subject: what size of data do others have experience with using rhipe?
parts:
I was curious if any other users could share what size of data they
have used Rhipe with and how their experience has been.

I am currently working with 2 TB of data, which is stored as 16K
sequence files at ~128 MB each.

When I run a job with this data as the input, it takes about 12-15
minutes just to set up the job with rhmr, with something like z <-
rhmr(..., ifolder="/inputdata/p*"). I am guessing that this is
because it needs to get a listing of all these files? Just checking
to see if this is normal behavior that others are experiencing or if I
should look into doing something about it.

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] what size of data do others have experience with using rhipe?
parts:
Yes the 16k entries causes the delay. Have you considered doing a one time identity mapreduce with a few number of reducers? Essentially redivide the 16k files into a smaller number of files.

I have some.jobs with 6k input files.

Saptarshi

messages.author: 1b02e64a42470974
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: what size of data do others have experience with using rhipe?
parts:
Hadoop performs way better with small number of large files!
(Large number of small files is a hadoop bottleneck.. )


It's easier to even consolidate the small files to a decent size
before running on hadoop -
Here's Nathanmarz' comment from yore -
http://blog.rapleaf.com/dev/2008/11/20/give-me-liberty-or-give-me-death-but-dont-give-me-small-files/

For the details of the sequence file organization see the Definitive
Guide or a similar description below:
http://www.cloudera.com/blog/2009/02/the-small-files-problem/
